Publish this project (the workspace, ~/projects/forge) to a new PRIVATE GitHub repository. Follow these steps in order and stop if one fails.

1. Secret scan. Run `gitleaks detect --source . --log-opts="--all" --redact -v` (scans all files and all git history) and
   `gitleaks detect --source . --no-git --redact`. If either reports any finding, STOP and report it. Do not push.
   Also confirm .gitignore excludes .venv/ and that `git status --short` is clean apart from your README change.
2. Edit README.md: add a section near the end titled "## How this was built". It must say, honestly and briefly:
   - The models doing the work are Meta's: Muse Glimmer 30B (open weights, the student, served with vLLM on Modal),
     Muse Spark Open (open weights, the teacher, on Baseten).
   - Muse Code (Meta's coding agent) built the test program: experiments/first-test/runner.py and test_runner.py, and
     the later fixes from CHANGES_SPEC.md. From now on all project code is built by Muse Code from written specs.
   - Claude (Anthropic) was used as a planning assistant: it wrote the plans, specs, exam jobs and checks
     (experiments/first-test/jobs.py, checks.py, PLAN.md), the wiki, and coordinated; commits made with it carry a
     "Co-Authored-By: Claude" line.
   - Muse Code published this repository.
   Do not change any other file.
3. Commit the README change with the message "README: how this was built (published by Muse Code)".
4. Create the repository and push: `gh repo create alyssaaa11/expertery --private --source . --remote origin --push`.
   It must be PRIVATE. Do not make anything public.
5. Verify: `gh repo view alyssaaa11/expertery --json visibility,url,defaultBranchRef` must show PRIVATE, and
   `git status -sb` must show the branch in sync with origin.
Reply with: the gitleaks results, the commit hash, the repo URL, its visibility, and anything you could not do.

Read text file `README.md`.
1|# Forge
2|
3|A private AI agent that becomes a pro at your company's tool. Muse Spark (the teacher) practises the tool, the real
4|results are checked automatically, and Glimmer (the student) is LoRA-trained on the correct attempts only. Each company
5|gets its own add-on file, running offline on its own servers.
6|
7|Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026 (Indie track, Push the Frontier). Submission due Nov 4, 18:00 CET.
8|
9|Status (2026-10-28 evening): first test done. Real gap: Spark Open 30/30 vs Glimmer + manual 20/30 (grey zone by the
10|rule, user decided **GO**). Spent ≈ $3.5 of $30. Next: factory (see `forge-wiki/wiki/status.md`, read it first each day).
11|
12|## Folders
13|| Folder | What goes in it |
14||---|---|
15|| `forge-wiki/` | the project's knowledge base (Obsidian vault) |
16|| `deploy/` | Glimmer on Modal |
17|| `docs/diagrams/` | the 6 Archify diagrams (open the `.html` files in a browser) |
18|| `specs/` | specs our agents write; Muse Code writes the code from them (project rule) |
19|| `scripts/` | setup checks (`check_cadquery.py`) |
20|| `data/` | practice jobs and good examples (fake data only) |
21|| `results/` | test results and scoreboards |
22|| `.venv/` | Python 3.12 with CadQuery 2.8.0 (system Python 3.15 has no CadQuery build) |
23|
24|## Diagrams, in reading order
25|1. `forge-explained`: what Forge is
26|2. `forge-pro-agent`: the design
27|3. `forge-use-cases`: who would use it
28|4. `forge-prepare`: the checklist before running
29|5. `forge-plan`: Oct 28 to Nov 4
30|6. `forge-factory`: what a company installs, and what leaves it
31|
32|## Main tool
33|CadQuery (Python CAD, exports STEP for factories). Backup: OpenSCAD.
34|
35|## Where the rest lives
36|All paths below were checked to exist on 2026-10-28.
37|
38|### Forge knowledge: `forge-wiki/` (in this folder)
39|- Start at `forge-wiki/index.md`. Design: `wiki/findings/forge-design-2026-10-28.md`. Plan, budget and GO rules:
40|  `wiki/decisions/forge-plan-2026-10-28.md`. Q&A: `wiki/findings/forge-questions-2026-10-28.md`. First Glimmer run:
41|  `wiki/findings/glimmer-test-1-2026-10-28.md`. Lessons: `wiki/lessons/lessons.md`.
42|
43|### Glimmer on Modal (Forge's own)
44|- `deploy/modal_glimmer.py`: app and secret `forge-glimmer`, volumes `forge-hf-cache` / `forge-vllm-cache`, one GPU at most.
45|- Server password: envsave `FORGE_GLIMMER_VLLM_API_KEY` (also stored in the Modal secret). Modal workspace `my-workspace`.
46|- Stop after every session: `modal app stop forge-glimmer`. Check spend: `modal billing summary`.
47|- Training example to base the LoRA spec on: https://modal.com/docs/examples/unsloth_finetune
48|
49|### Hackathon rules
50|- Rubric, prizes, problem statement, deadlines: `~/.hivey/agent/hiveyAgent-wiki/wiki/user/meta-hackathon-2026.md`
51|- Overview across the user's projects: `~/Obsidian-wikis/master/wiki/knowledge/meta-hackathon-herdshot-2026.md`
52|
53|### Meta model facts (learned in the earlier HerdShot project; background only)
54|- Muse Spark API (endpoint, prices, contributor tier, thinking eats max_tokens): `~/swarms/herdshot/herdshot-wiki/wiki/findings/meta-model-api.md`
55|- Muse models and tools (Glimmer, Spark Open on Baseten, Muse Code CLI): `~/swarms/herdshot/herdshot-wiki/wiki/findings/models-and-tools-2026-10-27.md`
56|- Keys (envsave names): `META_HERDSHOT_API_KEY` (Muse Spark; named for the earlier project, the same Meta account), `BASETEN_API_KEY` (Spark Open)
57|
58|### Research and origin
59|- Merged research report: `~/Research/2026-10-28-hackathon-final-validation/merged.md` (raw copies in `forge-wiki/raw/knowledge/`)
60|- Where the idea came from: `~/agents/superintel/reports/hackathon-software-ideas_2026-10-28.md`
61|
62|## Not researched yet (gaps)
63|- **SAM 3.1:** how to install and run it locally on this Mac, and what it adds beyond CadQuery's exact measurements.
64|  Needed before the result checker is designed.
65|- **Glimmer LoRA recipe:** the exact training settings and memory (Meta's post-training guide, Unsloth support for
66|  Glimmer). Needed for the Part B spec.
67|- **Muse Code headless use (`muse exec`):** flags, and whether it bills the Meta credit. Needed before the first build.
68|
69|## Check the setup
70|```bash
71|cd /tmp && ~/projects/forge/.venv/bin/python -I ~/projects/forge/scripts/check_cadquery.py
72|# expect: size mm: 20.0 20.0 20.0 and volume 7607.3 = expected
73|```
